summary: APM feed s117_double is degraded: 56.2% of TCP sessions are one-way and 11.3% of packets are duplicates, preventing complete bidirectional transaction analysis.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding only one direction for most flows to this APM port. With 72 of 128 TCP sessions (56.2%) showing single-direction traffic, this indicates asymmetric routing combined with per-direction load-balancing/filtering or a SPAN/mirror configured for one direction, where return traffic is sent to a different tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to correlate requests/responses and compute latency, error rate and transaction completion. One-way visibility causes broken transaction stitching, missing response times and under-reported errors.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow/session to the same APM tool port using flow-aware bidirectional hashing, ensuring complete request/response pairs for APM.

findings.root_cause: 11.3% duplicate packets (181 of 1605) indicates overlapping capture sources (e.g., SPAN from two switches or dual TAPs) aggregated in the packet broker without deduplication, delivering the same packet twice.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates inflate APM transaction counts, distort retransmission and latency calculations, and waste APM processing cycles and 10G port bandwidth even though full payload is not required.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to suppress identical packets within a short window before delivery, restoring accurate metrics and reducing load on APM.
